subject: Current-source compiler cache and native manifest-reader bytecode construction
claim: The existing current split-project build command completed all 13 steps on Windows and published a current-source analyzer/emitter checkpoint plus the maintained manifest-reader project's WVB. The emitter was compiled through symbol analysis, WIR analysis, and emission; its WVB and executable match the earlier read-through-tested emitter. The final manifest-reader WVB also matches the earlier Project 4 reader. Exact matching intermediate and native-image caches were reused, not relabeled as cold reconstruction.

runs.target: Current split-compiler development checkpoint and Seed bootstrap manifest-reader project

limitations: This is a Windows development construction checkpoint, not cold double-build, independent reproduction, new Debian qualification, installed promotion, or full compiler/library conformance.

The analyzer WVB and final reader analysis were exact cache hits. Bootstrap analyzer packaging reused the successful product from a prior five-minute attempt; that prior attempt timed out before completing the compiler set.

The approved run completed in approximately twelve minutes. Per-step measurements were available, but exact total wall time and peak working set were not recorded. The two construction branches ran concurrently.
Existing package migration working-tree edits and standalone Project 4 parser fixtures were not inputs to these compiler/reader projects and were not committed or qualified by this run.
The manifest reader was built as WVB, not newly packaged and executed. Equality with earlier reader bytecode is identity evidence, not a new runtime test.
Normal Build-Wvb routing, acquisition of the other admission products, Project 4 build-result caching, and installed toolchain delivery remain unfinished. No production artifact pin was changed.
